subject: DPIA onboarding & Art.28/30 evidence request — MediServe
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@mediserve.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: security@mediserve.com
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPIA + evidence ask for Redwood (MediServe onboarding)

Hi Jasmine / Neha,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood for our clinical-notes normalization pipeline. As part of our security & privacy intake we need the following items to complete our DPIA and legal review: 

- Completed DPIA questionnaire (attached) — could you confirm who on your side will complete the vendor sections?
- Article 30 processing ledger (exported CSV or spreadsheet) showing subprocessors, processing purposes, data categories, and transfer destinations
- Subprocessor roster (current) with locations and any subprocessors that have access to plaintext data
- SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) or ISO equivalent
- Evidence of keys and encryption handling (KMS console screenshots or equivalent) and a short explanation of key rotation/access controls

Can you also confirm whether Redwood uses any third-party vector DB or managed feature store that would be a separate subprocessor for embeddings? If so, please name them and indicate whether they can be restricted for EU-only customers.

Target timeline: we need the packet by July 7 to stay on schedule for our July 15 security committee. If there are items you can’t share publicly (e.g., KMS logs), tell us the minimal evidence you can provide and a contact to arrange secured access.

Questionnaire attached: Mediserve_DPIA_Questionnaire_v3.pdf

Best,
Laura Chen
Director, Information Security
MediServe Health

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai

Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPIA + evidence ask for Redwood (MediServe onboarding)

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list and for sending the questionnaire. We can cover everything on that list. High-level notes up front:

- Owner: I’ll be the primary point for the DPIA packet and will coordinate artifacts.
- Timeline: July 7 is achievable for the initial packet (redacted reports + ledger). Anything that requires secured sharing (KMS console screenshots, raw logs) we can schedule for a secured transfer the week of July 12.
- Vector DB: Redwood’s hosted inference path uses a managed embeddings cache for short-term KV only; we do not persist customer embeddings to third-party vector DBs by default. For customers who configure an external vector DB (managed by Redwood or customer), we document that as a subprocessor. I’ll confirm the exact partner names if any of your workloads will be configured that way.

I’ve attached a preliminary Art.30 ledger export (redwood_art30_ledger_2027-06.csv) which contains our current subprocessors and processing purposes. It’s a CSV export so you should be able to map columns to your questionnaire.

Would you be available for a short call on Friday 7/2 at 10am PT to run through any clarifying questions? If that slot doesn’t work we can do Monday 7/5.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer — Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_art30_ledger_2027-06.csv

Hi Laura — quick follow-up from our side with details on the artifacts we’ll provide and a couple of constraints: 

What we will provide by July 7 (redacted where appropriate):
- Art. 30 ledger CSV (attached) — includes subprocessors, subprocessor country, processing purpose, controller instructions mapping
- SOC 2 Type II report (PDF, redacted) — see attached SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf; we will also provide the security annex that maps controls to our products if you need it
- Subprocessor roster (separate sheet in the CSV) with an indication whether the subprocessors have access to cleartext customer data

What requires secured handling / separate onboarding: 
- KMS access and key management evidence — we cannot share raw KMS audit logs over email. We can provide screenshots (example attached: kms-access-screenshot.png) and we can set up a time-limited, secure transfer (SFTP or secure Drive with DLP) for extracts if you need more.
- For hosted deployments: some telemetry & batching services are run in managed clusters that rely on a small set of infra partners; details are in the Art.30 export. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can scope subprocessors differently — happy to confirm based on your chosen deployment mode.

Regarding your vector DB question: we do not wire a third-party vector DB into hosted inference by default. Some integrations (customer-requested) use Pinecone or Weaviate — if you want to enforce EU-only storage we can document that as a contractual restriction and limit the partner selection. That will require a brief config change and a note in the DPA addendum.

Call confirmation: I can do Friday 7/2 at 10am PT. Jasmine — can you send a calendar invite?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf, kms-access-screenshot.png

Thanks all — 10am PT works. A few clarifying items so we can prep: 

- Can you mark in the ledger which subprocessors have logical access to customer plaintext (i.e., decrypt for processing) vs. only encrypted metadata? That will speed our DPIA review.
- For Pinecone / Weaviate mention: do you have a policy on replay/retention for embeddings if a customer chooses an external vector DB? We need to know retention windows and deletion processes.
- On the SOC2: is there an NDA or secure portal we should use to access the full un-redacted report, or do you only provide redacted copies by default?

One more thing: our procurement team asked whether Redwood is willing to add a short DPA addendum clause allowing us to audit (remote, evidence-based) once per year for 90 days notice. If that is a hard no, please let us know so we can route accordingly.

Laura
